summary: Template assembly tool pack, stdlib only and deliberately free: it is mechanism, and gating the mechanism that makes an agent's output correct only makes free-tier output worse. tpl-build.py assembles one source template or an ordered block set into Markdown plus a self-contained HTML copy, resolving every declared parameter explicit value, then project store, then declared default, then ask — and a required parameter that reaches the end of that order with nothing to fill it is refused by name rather than substituted empty, which is the difference between a template that fails loudly and a document shipped with a hole in it. The template language is {{name}} substitution plus sections gated on `when: var in [literal, ...]` and nothing else: expressions, loops, filters, Mustache partials, dotted paths, YAML anchors, block scalars and every other construct are each refused by name, because the same assembler runs on behalf of other accounts and a general template language there is a server-side template injection surface. An assembly is blocks plus literal passthrough, because measured over the corpus blocks cover the envelope and the median template shares no bytes with any other: --use takes block references and .md file paths in one ordered list, and a section matching no block is assembled from literals rather than treated as an error. The Markdown to HTML renderer is partial on purpose and says so — headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, fenced code, blockquotes, links, emphasis — escaping everything else, and it runs two escaping paths that never meet: source text is escaped entity-preservingly, so the 58-file family that already stores <artefact_id> is not double-escaped into visible entities, while a substituted value is held as an opaque sentinel through the whole render and escaped unconditionally at the end, so it can neither open a tag nor forge a heading nor break out of a table cell, and only http, https, mailto and relative hrefs are ever resolved. A successful build then remembers what it was given: every --set or --values answer is written to the project store so the next build asks for less, while a value that came from a declared default is deliberately never persisted, because freezing a default means a later change to the block silently stops taking effect and nothing in the project explains why; --no-remember opts out. tpl-params.py is the ask channel: it lists every declared parameter with its type, requiredness, default and whether the project store already answers it, and emits as JSON exactly which parameters are unresolved and the question to ask for each, flagging a text parameter as prose an LLM composes rather than a value a user types. It manages the store at {project}/.faion/template-params.json and a sensitive parameter never reaches it: the store records that the parameter exists and its placeholder, never the value, and any value matching a known secret shape is refused whatever the declaration says.
